key_conventions: ICD cash interest and realized principal outside operating EV; tax conservatively payable on accrued income. No coupon after principal realization.

FY26 INR0.50 declared-dividend obligation paid in assumed30September2026 interval, before entry; no entitlement to post-record-date buyer. Counterfactual pre-record rescue shares receive equal entitlement.
No new ICD lending assumed. Existing repayments uncertain; no asserted fair value at book.
Pledged FD not spendable, OD continues at7.30%; orderly terminal FD/OD realization is conditional, shown separately.
Model operating reserve is analyst-selected, not observed distress. All required pre-entry and post-entry breaches suppress non-rescue returns.

Pre-receipt cash test pays all interval capex, positive WC investment, principal, tax, interest and claims before EBITDA/ICD/FD/disposal inflows; timing fraction sensitivity applies only to capex/WC. Base uses net operating cash after working capital, not all gross supplier/payroll payments upfront; separate0/50/100%gross-cost prefunding sensitivity changes funding timing only, not actual operating costs. No verified payment calendar is claimed.
Whole-share rescue placed before each deficient interval at fixed INR30.375 (25% discount to the INR40.50 reference), 3%fees. No permitted/committed issuance is asserted.
Operating lease rent is expensed; no second lease debt. Finance-lease receivables inside ONWC; no separate terminal value.
PPE/operating properties included in earnings EV, not added as assets. Resale proceeds reduce replacement cash cost.
Terminal EV is lower of EBIT multiple and maintenance-adjusted owner-cash multiple. No asset value on top of EV.
Term amortization beyond disclosed first-year current maturity is analyst approximation, explicitly stressed through funding; no refinancing assumed.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.content_markdown: **Hold — unresolved. Not an evidence-backed compounder.** Mangal combines IT hardware rentals, equipment resale and implementation/support. Revenue expanded strongly, but FY2026 core operating EBIT fell about 7% while other income, largely loans and deposits, supported reported profit. The central issue is whether replacement-intensive operations and ₹32.84 cr of extended unsecured loan assets produce collectible owner cash, not the headline P/E. Clean latest audit/IFC/trail and no FY2026 lender default are important positives, not substitutes for resolving material cash-flow/note bridges. The cutoff price is unverified; ₹40.50 is only a scenario reference. A fully hypothetical funded base returns 13.77%, below the 15% hurdle, but it requires ₹5.02 cr gross rescue and is not an ordinary valuation or financing recommendation. Thesis type: **conditional asset-recovery/operating special situation**, not proven recurring compounding. Reconciled cash flows, actual loan collections, productive fleet economics and executable market evidence would change the assessment. sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.content_markdown:
| Measure | Known weighted subtotal | Coverage | Missing-data bound | Raw/final | Override |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BQS | 4.2600 | 90.00% | 4.4–5.3 | NS / NS | CASH missing and G2 Hold; bounds are not scores; no renormalization |
| GQS | 5.4000 | 90.00% | 5.5–6.4 | NS / NS | CASH missing and G2 Hold; bounds are not scores; no renormalization |
| IAS | 0.0000 | 0.00% | 1.8–8.8 | NS / NS | G2/G4 Hold and missing Q/R/D/P/L; nested mathematical bounds only |

Weights are applied without redistributing unknown factors. Bounds put each missing factor at 1 or 10; they are not neutral imputations, confidence intervals or investable scores. IAS reuses unrounded final BQS only; its entire Q contribution is unknown, though nested bounds retain upstream information. R/D/P/L are NS because price/funding/execution evidence does not support an actual entry assessment. High structural impairment risk is described separately, not converted into a false price-specific D score.

| Factor | Score | Confidence | Evidence | Audit rationale and contrary evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GOV | 4 | Medium | E12, E14, E16, E17 | Large extended unsecured ICD exposure and repeated payment/disclosure weaknesses indicate weak allocation discipline. This is stewardship weakness, not proven fraud. Counter: Clean latest audit/IFC/trail, no FY2026 lender default or reported fraud, no promoter pledge; fee-based auditor resignation includes no denied-information allegation. |
| MOAT | 4 | Medium | E03, E04 | Vendor hardware is substitutable and customer/vendor concentration is material. Thin resale gross margin and declining rentals do not demonstrate persistent pricing power. Counter: Customer relationships, configuration/support and installed assets can create some switching friction; operating margins exceed pure distributors. |
| REV | 8 | Medium | E02, E07 | Preselected five-year operations CAGR 22.623% starts at 8; three-year 24.857% supports it. No trajectory adjustment; medium-history ceiling 8. Gross pass-through mix and lack of volume split are explicit. Counter: FY2026 rental revenue fell 16.65%; total expansion is not rental volume growth. FY2021 original/FY2022–24 restated accounting bases labelled, operations perimeter comparable. |
| DUR | 5 | Medium | E03, E19 | Enterprise IT rental, implementation and backup/cloud give accessible but competitive avenues; disclosed multi-city client expansion and equipment installation establish activity. Counter: No current customer cohorts, committed recurring backlog or utilization evidence; technology obsolescence and concentration constrain duration. |
| CAP | 4 | Medium | E06, E12 | Bottom-up FY2024–26 incremental NOPAT/IC~7.78% at 26% tax falls below reasoned 12–16% capital hurdle range; latest-year increment negative. Large 12% pretax ICD deployment yields only~9% after tax before credit loss. Counter: Current core NOPAT/average IC~22.8% and FY2024–25 incremental return were strong. New fleet ramp affects short-window returns; segment cross-check 7.37% supports direction rather than inventing precision. |
| CASH | NS | Low | E09, E10, E11, E18 | Reported cumulative CFO is high, but material CFS sign/classification, tax and noncash loan-capitalization questions prevent scoring sustainable conversion. Unknown is not a low or neutral cash score. Counter: Aggregate cash totals reconcile; audited clean controls and specific candidate reclassifications are retained. No claim of a definitive corrected CFO. |
| BAL | 4 | Medium | E12, E13 | Free cash is tiny, term maturities significant and FD-backed OD callable. Long-dated unsecured recoveries and replacement needs make funding sensitive. Counter: Pledged FD substantially covers OD; latest auditor reports no default and positive one-year liability assessment. Model reserve gaps are not observed default. |
| EXEC | 5 | Medium | E19, E05 | FY2026 reported growth exceeded 20% indication, with documented geographic and equipment milestones. Delivery is mixed because operating EBIT/rentals declined while assets expanded. Counter: Milestones do not prove utilization or project ROI; some total revenue delivery is evidenced, so no blanket execution failure. |
| EARN | 4 | Medium | E07, E08, E23 | Other income is over half PBT; core operating EBIT fell~7% while PAT rose. Historical share gains/bad debts and IPO share-base change weaken apparent growth. Counter: Reported EPS still rose and lower financing cost helps. Operational finance-lease interest retained rather than indiscriminately stripped. |
| R | NS | Low | E21, E22 | No authenticated cutoff entry price and material G2/funding conditions. Hypothetical rescue returns cannot support the canonical return score. Counter: Full dated return and 12/15/18% hurdle calculations are retained as conditional diagnostics, not discarded. |
| D | NS | Low | E12, E22 | Structural impairment risk is High, but downside at an actual entry price and executable financing remains unverified. Do not turn assumed-price stress into an unconditional score. Counter: Collateralized OD, productive assets and potential ICD repayment provide recoverable value; book assets are not a guaranteed liquidation floor. |

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.content_markdown:
Mangal acquires and rents computers, servers, storage and related IT hardware, resells equipment, and supplies implementation/configuration, backup/cloud and support services. The company was incorporated as Pathik Computer Systems Private Limited on 11 April 2011, renamed Mangal on 7 June 2012 and converted to public status on 26 October 2023. sections.content_markdown:
Demand access is plausible through enterprise equipment refresh, flexible rentals, configuration and managed backup/cloud, with disclosed clients across more than eight cities. This is a competitive opportunity, not a quantified addressable-market-to-market-share forecast. July 2025 automation and storage installation establish operating milestones; there is no auditable contracted recurring-revenue/utilization bridge. Management’s six-year useful life is an accounting estimate, not a guaranteed economic replacement cycle. Rental revenue/gross computer book fell from about 40% to 25%, a deployment/productivity proxy, not equipment utilization. The base model holds the gross fleet for two years while new capacity is absorbed, then grows it with 80% rental plus 20% service growth; the bear allows only one year idle deployment and faster replacement. sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.content_markdown:
The strongest bear case is that services growth conceals deteriorating rental productivity while book-value loan assets are less collectible than their coupon suggests. Faster hardware replacement,90 daycollections, weaker margins and delayed/haircut ICD recovery occur together. Bank collateral may repay the OD but not make the pledged FD freely available for fleet renewal. Continued statutory obligations, callable finance and dividends consume liquidity before customer receipts. Equity then bears new-share dilution, issue costs and an impaired operating franchise.

The funded bear requires ₹41.75 cr gross equity and 101.02% full-history share expansion. Terminal price ₹3.67 is about 90.95% below the assumed entry reference before considering shutdown uncertainty. Without the invented rescue, funding fails and no investor return is presented. Even the rescued terminal residual is not a legal liquidation valuation: employee termination, customer migration, lease exit, hardware disposal costs and enforceable collateral/ICD collections are not independently established.

**Impairment risk: High; potentially Severe if loan recovery and operating renewal fail together.** The thesis-break variable is cash actually received from counterparties relative to replacement and near-term claims, not whether reported PAT remains positive. The positive countercase is genuine service scaling, effective fleet utilization, clean latest controls and punctual cash repayment. Those events can improve value, but cannot be presumed from contractual maturity or audited book classification. The required uniform revenue growth runs from 31 March 2026, about 5.56 years, not a hidden extra five years after entry. They assume recovered loans, funded capital needs and sustained exit multiples. Large scale is mathematically possible in the solver but not evidenced by current contracts, customer diversification or project returns. **Neither 5× nor 10× is an evidence-backed central thesis.** Solutions are conditional stress diagnostics, not target prices.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.content_markdown:
**Classification: Hold — unresolved. Research priority, not eligible for investment consideration or quality ranking.** BQS/GQS/IAS are NS with exact missing-data bounds, and the decisive override is G2/G4 rather than a claimed governance fraud. Compounder designation fails because GOV/MOAT/CAP are below 7, CASH is NS and critical gates remain unresolved. A low headline P/E does not establish a value bargain when nonoperating loan income, replacement capex and liquidity dominate.

Before an investment-grade reassessment: reconcile the material cash-flow/disposal/tax mappings; establish realizable and dated ICD collections; demonstrate fleet earning utilization and sustainable replacement cash; prove funding through the cash trough; verify current BSE price/lot and implementable exit capacity. The assumed-price base’s 15% hurdle value ₹38.57 is not a buy level because it assumes synthetic financing and unresolved cash economics. Even a cheaper price would not by itself clear G2/G4. No actual holding, tax basis or portfolio weight is known, so no exit count, allocation or trade is prescribed.

summary: **Hold — unresolved. Not an evidence-backed compounder.** Mangal combines IT hardware rentals, equipment resale and implementation/support. Revenue expanded strongly, but FY2026 core operating EBIT fell about 7% while other income, largely loans and deposits, supported reported profit. The central issue is whether replacement-intensive operations and ₹32.84 cr of extended unsecured loan assets produce collectible owner cash, not the headline P/E. Clean latest audit/IFC/trail and no FY2026 lender default are important positives, not substitutes for resolving material cash-flow/note bridges. The cutoff price is unverified; ₹40.50 is only a scenario reference. A fully hypothetical funded base returns 13.77%, below the 15% hurdle, but it requires ₹5.02 cr gross rescue and is not an ordinary valuation or financing recommendation. Thesis type: **conditional asset-recovery/operating special situation**, not proven recurring compounding. Reconciled cash flows, actual loan collections, productive fleet economics and executable market evidence would change the assessment.
